question: Which classic 1950s sitcom starred bandleader Ricky Ricardo and his scheming redheaded wife, who always had some “splainin'” to do?
hint: The title is a three-word love letter that ends with the redhead's first name.
funFact: When she had her TV baby in 1953, 44 million people tuned in: more than watched Eisenhower's inauguration the next day!

question: Which mop-topped band made its live US TV debut on The Ed Sullivan Show in February 1964, setting off a nationwide shriek?
hint: Four lads from Liverpool. Their name is an insect, creatively misspelled.
funFact: About 73 million Americans tuned in: roughly 60% of every TV switched on that night. Beatlemania was officially contagious.

question: Beam me up! In the original Star Trek, what is the name of Captain Kirk's starship?
hint: Registry NCC-1701. Its name also means a bold new business venture.
funFact: The original series was canceled after just three seasons (1966–69)… then boldly went on to launch one of TV's biggest franchises.

question: Which grumpy Sesame Street Muppet lives in a trash can and absolutely loves it there?
hint: He's green, he's grumpy, and his pet worm is named Slimey.
funFact: Puppeteer Caroll Spinney played this grump AND sunny Big Bird from 1969 to 2018. Talk about range!

question: Which boxer, born Cassius Clay, promised to “float like a butterfly, sting like a bee”?
hint: He called himself “The Greatest,” and his famous last name is just three letters.
funFact: In 1996 he surprised the whole world by lighting the Olympic cauldron at the Atlanta Games. Goosebumps, guaranteed.

question: What 1975 Steven Spielberg thriller made an entire generation afraid to go back in the water?
hint: Dun-dun… dun-dun… dun-dun-dun-dun! You're gonna need a bigger boat.
funFact: The crew nicknamed the mechanical shark “Bruce,” after Spielberg's lawyer. It kept breaking down, which is why you barely see it!

question: On which TV game show does the announcer yell “Come on down!” at a wildly excited audience member?
hint: Guess what it costs without going over! Home of Plinko and the Showcase.
funFact: Bob Barker hosted it for 35 years (1972–2007) and signed off by reminding everyone to have their pets spayed or neutered.

question: Which brothers' group sang “Stayin' Alive” while John Travolta strutted through Saturday Night Fever?
hint: Three Gibb brothers, sky-high falsettos, and a name that sounds like two letters.
funFact: Its beat sits right in the 100–120 bpm range for CPR chest compressions, so it's used to teach CPR. Literally stayin' alive!

question: In Top Gun (1986), what is Tom Cruise's hotshot pilot call sign?
hint: It means an unorthodox rule-breaker. Very on brand. His wingman is Goose.
funFact: Talk about a long taxi down the runway: the sequel arrived 36 years later, in 2022.

question: In Super Mario Bros., what is the name of Mario's taller, greener, forever-second-billed brother?
hint: Starts with L, and he has a whole Mansion full of ghosts to clean.
funFact: Mario's debut was Donkey Kong (1981), where he was just called “Jumpman.” Not exactly a superstar name.

question: What twisting puzzle cube, invented in Hungary, had the whole world quietly peeling off stickers around 1980?
hint: Named after its inventor, Ernő. Six faces, nine squares each, zero patience.
funFact: It can be scrambled 43 quintillion ways, yet every position can be solved in 20 moves or fewer. Even the one in your junk drawer.

question: Which Friends character greets everyone with a smooth “How you doin'?”
hint: He does NOT share food. Plays Dr. Drake Ramoray on Days of Our Lives.
funFact: Matt LeBlanc took him solo in the spin-off Joey (2004–06). Two whole seasons, and he still didn't share his food.

question: In The Lion King (1994), what's the name of Simba's villainous uncle, the worst relative at any family reunion?
hint: He sings “Be Prepared.” One syllable, like the mark over his eye.
funFact: Mufasa was voiced by James Earl Jones, also the voice of Darth Vader. So Simba's dad and Luke's dad sound exactly alike!

question: Which basketball legend was nicknamed “His Airness,” and sold a LOT of sneakers?
hint: Six titles with the Chicago Bulls, wore No. 23, and teamed up with Bugs Bunny in Space Jam.
funFact: Nike launched his first signature sneaker, the Air Jordan, in 1985, and it's still flying off the shelves.

question: Down in Bikini Bottom, what's the name of SpongeBob SquarePants's pet snail?
hint: He meows like a cat. Four letters, rhymes with “scary.”
funFact: Creator Stephen Hillenburg taught marine biology before he animated. So a real ocean expert signed off on a talking sponge.

question: In Shrek (2001), what does Shrek say ogres have in common with onions?
hint: Donkey suggests cakes and parfaits instead. Everybody loves parfaits!
funFact: Shrek won the very first Oscar for Best Animated Feature, beating Monsters, Inc. Ogres 1, Monsters 0.

question: Which actor played genius billionaire Tony Stark in the Iron Man films?
hint: He also played Sherlock Holmes, and his name ends with “Jr.”
funFact: Iron Man (2008) was the very first Marvel Cinematic Universe film: the snowball that started the avalanche.

question: In the US version of The Office, in which Pennsylvania city does Michael Scott run the Dunder Mifflin branch?
hint: Nicknamed “the Electric City,” and it rhymes with “Canton.”
funFact: It was adapted from the British original by Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant (2001). Bears. Beets. Battlestar Galactica.

question: Which talk-show host shouted “You get a car! You get a car!” at her entire studio audience in 2004?
hint: Her show ran 25 seasons. A one-name superstar: five letters, starts with O.
funFact: All 276 people in the audience got a brand-new Pontiac G6. Best Secret Santa in history.

question: In Despicable Me (2010), what are Gru's little yellow, goggle-wearing, banana-obsessed helpers called?
hint: Three famous ones are Kevin, Stuart and Bob. “Bello!”
funFact: Co-director Pierre Coffin voices most of them, in gibberish sprinkled with real Spanish, French and Italian. Banana!

question: In which blocky building game do players dodge hissing, exploding green Creepers?
hint: Its default heroes are Steve and Alex, and absolutely everything is made of cubes.
funFact: Microsoft bought its maker, Mojang, for $2.5 billion in 2014. Not bad for a game about digging holes.

question: On July 21, 2023, moviegoers paired pink, sparkly Barbie with which very NOT pink blockbuster released the same day?
hint: Christopher Nolan's three-hour epic about the man behind the atomic bomb.
funFact: Fans called the double bill “Barbenheimer,” and the not-pink half went on to win Best Picture.

question: Which city hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics? Ooh la la!
hint: It last hosted exactly 100 years earlier, in 1924. Croissant, anyone?
funFact: It was the first Summer Olympics opening ceremony held outside a stadium: athletes paraded on boats along the Seine. Very wet, very chic.

question: Which deadpan Addams Family daughter got her own Netflix series in 2022, starring Jenna Ortega?
hint: Her brother is Pugsley, and she's named after a day of the week. The middle one.
funFact: Jenna Ortega choreographed the viral dance scene herself, set to The Cramps' “Goo Goo Muck.” Then the entire internet copied it.

question: Which chatty breakfast cereal has three elf mascots named Snap, Crackle and Pop?
hint: Pour on the milk and listen closely. Also the secret to marshmallow treats.
funFact: In the 1950s the trio briefly gained a fourth elf in ads, named Pow. Snap, Crackle, Pop… Pow? Pow got cut.

question: Which Danish company makes the colorful plastic bricks that ambush bare feet every Christmas morning?
hint: Everything is awesome! Four letters, and the little yellow minifigures have claw hands.
funFact: The name comes from the Danish “leg godt,” meaning “play well.” Stepping on one barefoot does not count as playing well.

question: Which candy's famous slogan promises it “melts in your mouth, not in your hand”?
hint: Its mascots include Red, Yellow and a very sassy Green.
funFact: The two M's stand for founders Forrest Mars and Bruce Murrie. Mars & Murrie: one sweet partnership.

question: Shaken, not stirred: which actor first played James Bond on the big screen, in Dr. No (1962)?
hint: This Scotsman delivered milk in Edinburgh long before he ordered martinis.
funFact: Ian Fleming borrowed the name James Bond from an American bird expert. The real Bond studied birds, not villains.

question: What 34-letter word did Mary Poppins sing about in 1964? (Spelling it is optional. Saying it is mandatory.)
hint: “Even though the sound of it is something quite atrocious…” It starts with “Super.”
funFact: Mary Poppins was Julie Andrews's very first film, and it won her the Best Actress Oscar. Practically perfect in every way.

question: To which US president did Marilyn Monroe famously breathe “Happy Birthday” in 1962?
hint: The gala came 10 days before his 45th birthday. Known by three initials.
funFact: Her sparkly, skin-tight gown sold at auction in 2016 for about $4.8 million. That's a LOT of birthday.

question: Which Korean War Army-hospital comedy said goodbye in 1983 with a finale watched by about 106 million Americans?
hint: Alan Alda played Hawkeye Pierce, and the title is full of asterisks.
funFact: The series ran 11 seasons, more than three times as long as the Korean War itself. Longest tour of duty ever.

question: Which Swedish group won Eurovision in 1974 with “Waterloo,” then never stopped getting played at weddings?
hint: Mamma Mia! The band's name is made from its members' first initials.
funFact: In 2022 they launched ABBA Voyage in London, a concert starring digital “ABBAtars,” so the real band never has to leave the house.

question: In Star Wars (1977), what's the name of Han Solo's ship, the one Luke calls “a piece of junk”?
hint: It made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs. Think a thousand years and a bird of prey.
funFact: Harrison Ford was working as a carpenter between acting jobs before Star Wars made him a star. Talk about a career renovation!

question: What 1972 Atari arcade game had players bat a blip back and forth with two on-screen paddles?
hint: Basically electronic table tennis. Its name is the second half of a sport.
funFact: The first test machine, in a California bar, “broke down” because its coin box was overflowing with quarters. Best problem ever.

question: Which soft drink's 1971 TV ad featured a hilltop choir singing “I'd like to teach the world to sing”?
hint: Mad Men's final episode ends with this ad. Also the drink in Santa's ads since the 1930s.
funFact: The jingle was re-recorded as a full song, “I'd Like to Teach the World to Sing (In Perfect Harmony),” and became a hit single. Earworm confirmed.

question: Great Scott! In Back to the Future, how fast must the DeLorean go to travel through time?
hint: Two identical digits. It also needs 1.21 gigawatts!
funFact: Eric Stoltz was first cast as Marty McFly and filmed for weeks before Michael J. Fox replaced him. Somebody really did change the past!

question: In 1980's “Miracle on Ice,” a team of US college hockey players stunned which heavily favored nation?
hint: Al Michaels: “Do you believe in miracles? Yes!” The opponent was a Cold War superpower.
funFact: Plot twist: it wasn't the gold-medal game! The US clinched gold two days later by beating Finland.

question: What egg-shaped digital pet from Japan beeped all day to be fed and cleaned up after, or it would die?
hint: Bandai released it in 1996, and lots of schools banned it from classrooms.
funFact: The name blends the Japanese word for egg, “tamago,” with the English word “watch.” Babysitting, but on a keychain.

question: Disney released Toy Story (1995), the first fully computer-animated feature, but which studio actually made it?
hint: Its logo stars a hopping desk lamp that squashes the letter I.
funFact: Steve Jobs bought it from Lucasfilm in 1986; Disney bought it outright for $7.4 billion in 2006. To infinity and beyond!

question: What was Sony's very first home video game console?
hint: Launched in Japan in December 1994. Its buttons: triangle, circle, X and square.
funFact: It grew out of a failed deal to build a CD-ROM add-on for Nintendo's Super NES. Nintendo's loss, Sony's level-up!

question: Which Nintendo console, launched in 2006, had whole families swinging motion-sensing remotes to play bowling and tennis?
hint: Code-named “Revolution,” and its remote came with a wrist strap for a very good reason.
funFact: After reports of remotes flying out of hands and into TVs, Nintendo swapped in 3.2 million sturdier wrist straps. Bowl responsibly!

question: What Australian cartoon follows a puppy, her little sister Bingo and their endlessly patient dad, Bandit?
hint: Their mum is Chilli, and every episode is a game like “Keepy Uppy” or “Magic Xylophone.”
funFact: The title pup is a Blue Heeler, and the show is made in Brisbane by Ludo Studio. For real life!

question: What's the name of the hidden, high-tech African nation in Black Panther (2018)? Cross your arms if you know it!
hint: It's rich in vibranium, and its salute comes with a shout of “… Forever!”
funFact: Black Panther was the first superhero film ever nominated for the Best Picture Oscar. Capes: finally invited to the fancy party.

question: In 2015, the internet nearly broke over a dress that lots of people swore was white and gold. What colors was it REALLY?
hint: Its maker, the UK store Roman Originals, settled it: two dark colors.
funFact: Roman Originals later made a one-off white-and-gold version and auctioned it for the charity Comic Relief. Everybody wins!

question: In 2012, which K-pop song became the first YouTube video to hit one billion views, and got everyone riding an invisible horse?
hint: Its singer is PSY, and the title name-drops a fancy Seoul neighborhood.
funFact: The title pokes fun at the flashy, newly rich lifestyle of Seoul's Gangnam district. Giddy-up!

question: Which British singer named her albums 19, 21, 25 and 30, making every release feel like a birthday party?
hint: Her hits include “Rolling in the Deep” and “Hello… it's me.”
funFact: Her James Bond theme “Skyfall” won the Oscar for Best Original Song. Licensed to thrill.

question: Which Kansas City Chiefs tight end began dating Taylor Swift in 2023, making football Sundays extremely sparkly?
hint: He wears No. 87 and hosts the New Heights podcast with his brother Jason.
funFact: Before they met, he went to her concert hoping to hand her a friendship bracelet with his phone number on it. Smooth… eventually.

question: What 2021 Korean Netflix drama has cash-strapped contestants play a deadly version of Red Light, Green Light?
hint: Green tracksuits, pink-suited guards, and one very creepy giant doll.
funFact: Star Lee Jung-jae became the first Asian actor to win the Emmy for Lead Actor in a Drama Series. Green light for history!

question: What daily five-letter guessing game did The New York Times buy in 2022, flooding group chats with green squares?
hint: Green means right spot, yellow means wrong spot, and the name puns on its creator's surname.
funFact: Software engineer Josh Wardle made it as a gift for his partner, and the name is a pun on his surname. Sweetest. Puzzle. Ever.

question: Which 2025 Netflix animated movie gave us the chart-topping song “Golden,” and every kid's new favorite singalong?
hint: Rumi, Mira and Zoey are pop idols by day and fight monsters by night.
funFact: “Golden,” sung by the film's fictional girl group HUNTR/X, hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in August 2025. Not bad for a band that isn't real!

question: Which brand's 40-ounce “Quencher” tumbler became the must-have (in every color) craze of 2023?
hint: Same name as hockey's most famous Cup. Making vacuum bottles since 1913.
funFact: After a viral video showed one surviving a car fire with ice still rattling inside, the company bought the owner a new car. Ice cold!

question: On the classic US Monopoly board, which property is the most expensive to buy (and the most painful to land on)?
hint: Dark blue, right before “Go.” In Atlantic City, you'd stroll along it by the beach.
funFact: The street names come from Atlantic City, New Jersey, and on the UK board this pricey spot is called Mayfair.

question: On Gilligan's Island, what was the name of the tour boat whose “three-hour tour” went very, very wrong?
hint: Named after a tiny fish. Not the most confidence-inspiring name for a boat.
funFact: Creator Sherwood Schwartz reportedly named it after FCC chairman Newton Minow, who'd called TV “a vast wasteland.” Revenge, by shipwreck!

question: The Etch A Sketch, a hit toy launched in 1960, was invented by an electrician from which country? Shake it and guess!
hint: Its inventor called it “the Magic Screen” in his own language: the language of love.
funFact: André Cassagnes called it L'Écran Magique; the Ohio Art Company renamed it Etch A Sketch. Shake to erase: no crumbs!

question: Which folk singer shocked purist fans by plugging in and “going electric” at the 1965 Newport Folk Festival?
hint: He later won the Nobel Prize in Literature. The times, they were a-changin'.
funFact: Timothée Chalamet played him in the 2024 film A Complete Unknown, and did his own singing, guitar and harmonica.

question: What 1975 fad gift came in a box with breathing holes and a training manual, but never needed feeding or walks?
hint: It was VERY good at “sit” and “stay.” “Fetch,” not so much.
funFact: Its creator, California ad man Gary Dahl, became a millionaire almost overnight. Selling rocks. In a box.

question: Which tennis champion beat Bobby Riggs in straight sets in the 1973 “Battle of the Sexes” match?
hint: Her first name is a Michael Jackson song; her last name is pure royalty.
funFact: An estimated 90 million people watched worldwide, and Emma Stone played her in the 2017 film Battle of the Sexes. Game, set, history!

question: In E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982), what candy does Elliott use to lure E.T., in the sweetest product placement ever?
hint: Peanut-butter candy in orange, yellow and brown. Not the cups: the little ones.
funFact: Mars reportedly passed on putting M&M's in the movie, so Hershey's candy got the part instead, and its sales soared. Oops!

question: Tetris got its name from the Greek “tetra” (four) plus which sport, creator Alexey Pajitnov's favorite?
hint: Grab a racket! Like Tetris, it starts with “Te.”
funFact: Pajitnov made it in Moscow in 1984; in 1989 it came packed with the Game Boy in the US, and nobody looked up again.

question: What was the first music video MTV played when it launched in 1981? (Spoiler: the title was a little smug.)
answer: “Video Killed the Radio Star” by The Buggles
hint: A 1979 UK No. 1 by The Buggles about one medium wiping out another. Oh-a-oh!
funFact: MTV's very first words on air were “Ladies and gentlemen, rock and roll.” Radio, for the record, is still doing fine.

question: Apple's famous “1984” Super Bowl ad was directed by which big-shot film director?
hint: He also directed Alien, Blade Runner and Gladiator. Are you not entertained?
funFact: The ad launched the Macintosh and aired nationally only once, during Super Bowl XVIII. Once was enough!

question: In Ghostbusters (1984), what giant, smiling, sailor-suited monster stomps through New York at the climax?
hint: Ray pictured the most harmless thing ever. Also great in s'mores and hot cocoa.
funFact: The gooey “melted marshmallow” that splattered the city and the cast was really shaving cream. Ghostbusting: surprisingly well groomed.

question: Which internet company's “You've got mail!” greeting inspired the title of a 1998 Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan film? (Cue the dial-up screech.)
hint: It mailed out millions of free trial discs. Three letters.
funFact: The famous voice belonged to Elwood Edwards, whose wife worked at the company. Talk about keeping it in the family!

question: What was Amazon's original name when Jeff Bezos founded it in 1994? (It didn't last long.)
hint: It came from a magician's magic word… and sounded a bit spooky over the phone.
funFact: His lawyer misheard it as “cadaver,” so Bezos renamed it after the world's biggest river. Spooky save!

question: Which 1990s boy band's name is a sneaky play on the last letters of its original members' first names?
hint: Justin Timberlake was a member, and their name means perfectly together.
funFact: The name came from Justin Timberlake's mom, who said their voices sounded so “in sync.” Thanks, Mom!

question: Who won the very first season of American Idol in 2002, and has been a superstar ever since?
hint: Her later hits include “Since U Been Gone,” and now she has her own talk show.
funFact: The original judges were Simon Cowell, Paula Abdul and Randy Jackson. So yes, she survived Simon. Dawg!

question: Being “Rickrolled” means being tricked into watching the video for which 1987 song? (We promise this isn't one.)
answer: “Never Gonna Give You Up” by Rick Astley
hint: Rick Astley's No. 1 in the UK and the US. Rick makes several very firm promises.
funFact: In 2008 Astley pulled a real-life Rickroll, popping out of a float in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to lip-sync it.

question: The first video ever uploaded to YouTube, “Me at the zoo” (2005), shows a co-founder standing in front of which animals?
hint: Filmed at the San Diego Zoo. The co-founder admires their really, really long trunks.
funFact: Jawed Karim's 19-second clip went up on April 23, 2005. Billions of cat videos later, it all started with these guys.

question: Which Las Vegas band sings the 2000s anthem “Mr. Brightside,” the song every party still screams along to?
hint: Frontman Brandon Flowers. Their name sounds scary, but they're very nice.
funFact: It has spent 500+ weeks in the UK Top 100, longer than any song ever, yet it never hit No. 1. Its peak? No. 10.

question: What is golfer Tiger Woods's real first name? (No, his birth certificate does not say “Tiger.”)
hint: It starts with E for his dad, Earl, and ends with K for his mom, Kultida.
funFact: In 1997, aged 21, he became the youngest-ever Masters champion, and won by a record 12 strokes. Roar!

question: Which emoji did Oxford Dictionaries crown its 2015 Word of the Year, despite it not being a word at all?
hint: One in five emojis sent in the UK that year was this one. LOL, but make it cry.
funFact: It was the first time a pictograph, not a word, won Word of the Year. The dictionary folks laughed till they cried.

question: In Downton Abbey, what is the surname of the Earl of Grantham's very, very posh family?
hint: Lady Mary, Lady Edith and Lady Sybil share it. It's also the town where Gatwick Airport is.
funFact: The grand house is really Highclere Castle in Hampshire, England, and a real Earl and Countess still live there.

question: In the Broadway musical Hamilton, which character narrates much of the story and ends up facing Hamilton in a fatal duel?
hint: Thomas Jefferson's first vice president. “Talk less, smile more.” Pardon me, are you… sir?
funFact: Hamilton won 11 Tony Awards in 2016, and Leslie Odom Jr. won Best Actor for this role. He was in the room where it happened!

question: In 2023, who became the first Asian woman to win the Best Actress Oscar, for Everything Everywhere All at Once?
hint: She swung swords in Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon and starred in Crazy Rich Asians.
funFact: She was crowned Miss Malaysia in 1983, then became an action star famous for doing her own stunts.

question: Beyoncé won her first Album of the Year Grammy in 2025 for which country-flavored album? Yee-haw!
hint: It includes her cover of “Jolene,” and the title pairs a ranch hand with her married name.
funFact: It also made her the first Black artist to win the Grammy for Best Country Album. Giddy-up!
